export.done.heading: The file was made
export.done.master: The file does not open with your master password. A later change of the master password does not change this file.
export.done.password: The file opens only with the export password you just chose. Ferret does not keep it and cannot recover it.
export.done.saved: Your browser saves the file where you choose or in its download folder. Look for the name that starts with ferret-export and ends with .ferretexport.
export.encrypted.heading: Encrypted export
export.encrypted.intro: The file is sealed with an export password. Without that password it cannot be opened, and nobody can recover it for you, not even the server. Store the file and the password in different places.
export.encrypted.master_help: Asked for again, because an export takes every secret in the vault with it.
export.encrypted.password_help: At least 12 characters, and not the same as your master password. This is the password that opens the file. Making the key takes some seconds and a lot of memory on purpose: it is what makes a stolen file hard to guess into.
export.encrypted.secret_key_help: This device does not remember the secret key. Type it from page 1 of your emergency sheet.
export.error.export_item_unreadable: An item could not be read, so no file was made. Sync again and try once more; if it stays, tell whoever runs the server.
export.error.input_same_as_master_passwo: The export password is the same as your master password. Choose a different one.
export.error.kdf_out_of_memory: This browser could not set aside the 256 MiB the key needs. Close other tabs or try another browser or device. No file was made.
export.error.kdf_out_of_range: The key settings were below what an export needs. No file was made.
export.error.nothing_to_export: This device holds no items to export yet. Wait for the first sync and try again.
export.error.too_large: The vault is larger than one export file can hold. No file was made.
export.error.unsupported: An item is in a newer format that a CSV file cannot hold without losing fields. Use JSON or the encrypted file.
export.heading: Export
export.intro: Take a copy of your vault with you. The encrypted file is a backup you keep yourself, apart from the server: it opens with an export password that you choose now, and it can be opened again in Ferret. A plain export is for moving to another service and is not encrypted.
export.last.date: Last encrypted export on this device: {date}.
export.last.never: You have not made an encrypted export on this device yet.
export.plain.busy: Checking your master password and reading the items...
export.plain.confirm: I understand that the file is not encrypted and that anyone who gets it can read all my passwords
export.plain.dialog_body: The file will hold all your passwords and notes in plain text. Make it only if you are about to move to another service, and delete it for good afterwards.
export.plain.dialog_title: Save an unencrypted copy of your vault?
export.plain.done_csv: CSV: values that start with =, +, - or @ got an apostrophe in front, so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas. Passkeys are not in a CSV file.
export.plain.done_items: Your browser saved the file. Delete it for good as soon as you have moved your data, and empty the trash.
export.plain.format_csv: CSV (logins and notes, for a spreadsheet or another service)
export.plain.heading: Plain export
export.plain.intro: A readable copy for moving to another service. It is not encrypted: it holds every password and note as plain text.
export.plain.passkeys_help: JSON only. A passkey's private key lets whoever has it sign in as you. CSV never has passkeys.
export.plain.secret_key_help: This device does not remember the secret key. Type it from page 1 of your emergency sheet.
export.plain.warning_files: Anyone who gets the file can read everything in it. Your computer may index it for search, show previews of it, copy it to a synced folder or include it in a backup, and sync tools may send it elsewhere. Save it in a folder you control that is not synced, use it, and delete it for good when you are done.
export.plain.warning_sync: Choose a folder that is not synced to the cloud. The browser decides where the file goes unless it asks you; check where it landed.
export.progress.saving: Handing the file to your browser...
export.progress.stretching: Making the key from the export password. This takes some seconds and uses 256 MiB of memory.
export.readiness.ack: Export anyway, I know the file may be missing recent changes
export.readiness.behind: This device could not confirm that it has read the newest state of the server, so the file may be missing items that were added or changed elsewhere.
export.readiness.checking: Checking that this device is up to date with the server...
export.readiness.ok: This device is up to date with the server and has no changes waiting.
export.readiness.pending: {count} item(s) have changes that the server has not accepted yet. They are not in the file as you see them on screen.
export.readiness.warning_heading: The file may not hold your newest changes
export.reminder.label: Export reminder
export.reminder.never: You have not made an encrypted export yet. Take one now and keep it apart from the server.
export.reminder.text: Your last encrypted export was on {date}. Take a new one so a copy of your vault is always in your own hands.
export.title: Export
